grammar.title: Keep both sides of a comparison
grammar.formation: Verb / i-adjective plain attributive form + 一方（で）; na-adjective + な / である一方（で）; noun + の / である一方（で）. 一方で can also introduce a new sentence.
grammar.explanation: 一方で places another aspect or side beside the first. It can compare two people’s approaches or two effects of one approach. The second clause does not erase the first. A contrast may have favourable and unfavourable sides, but this is not a compulsory positive-negative formula. Here a pause helps questions while interrupting the film’s flow.
grammar.example: 質問しやすい一方で、話の流れが途切れる。
grammar.translation: It’s easier to ask questions, while the flow of the story is interrupted.

examples.ja: {質問|しつもん}しやすい{一方|いっぽう}で、{話|はなし}の{流|なが}れが{途切|とぎ}れる。
examples.en: It’s easier to ask questions, while the flow of the story is interrupted.

examples.ja: ユイは{途中|とちゅう}で{止|と}めたい。{一方|いっぽう}で、{森|もり}さんは{全編|ぜんぺん}を{先|さき}に{見|み}たい。
examples.en: Yui wants to pause partway through. Mori, on the other hand, wants to watch the whole film first.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}は{明瞭|めいりょう}な{一方|いっぽう}で、{少|すこ}し{長|なが}い。
examples.en: The explanation is clear, but it’s a little long.

grammar.mistake: Do not choose 一方で or 反面 as uniquely correct solely because one clause is negative. Read both clauses and the stated comparison.

grammar.title: Notice another side of the same approach
grammar.formation: Verb / i-adjective attributive form + 反面; na-adjective + な / である反面; noun + である反面. その反面 can start a contrasting clause.
grammar.explanation: 反面 presents another, contrasting side. In this essay the same pause creates room for a question but may break immersion. It often discusses a benefit and a drawback; it does not require that order in every use. Its scope can overlap with 一方で, so tasks identify the actual effects rather than testing an invented universal dividing line.
grammar.example: 区切りで止めると質問しやすい反面、映画に没頭しにくくなる。
grammar.translation: Pausing at a break makes it easier to ask questions, but it can make it harder to get absorbed in the film.

examples.ja: {区切|くぎ}りで{止|と}めると{質問|しつもん}しやすい{反面|はんめん}、{映画|えいが}に{没頭|ぼっとう}しにくくなる。
examples.en: Pausing at a break makes it easier to ask questions, but it can make it harder to get absorbed in the film.

examples.ja: {全編|ぜんぺん}を{先|さき}に{見|み}ると{流|なが}れがつかめる。その{反面|はんめん}、{途中|とちゅう}の{疑問|ぎもん}を{忘|わす}れることもある。
examples.en: Watching the whole film first lets you follow its flow. On the other hand, you may forget a question you had partway through.

examples.ja: この{方法|ほうほう}は{有効|ゆうこう}な{反面|はんめん}、{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.en: This method is effective, but it takes time.

grammar.mistake: Attach な to an ordinary na-adjective here: 有効な反面. Both effects belong to the stated method; do not assign one to a different author.

grammar.title: Read the preferred alternative
grammar.formation: むしろ + clause; X より（も）むしろ Y.
grammar.explanation: むしろ marks an alternative judged more appropriate than the first idea, or corrects a characterisation. Here Mori favours watching the whole film first, rather than pausing at each chapter. The word alone does not show why; read the following reason. It is not a simple replacement for a contrast word meaning “however.”
grammar.example: 途中で何度も止めるより、むしろ最後まで見たい。
grammar.translation: Rather than pause repeatedly, I’d prefer to watch to the end.

examples.ja: {途中|とちゅう}で{何度|なんど}も{止|と}めるより、むしろ{最後|さいご}まで{見|み}たい。
examples.en: Rather than pause repeatedly, I’d prefer to watch to the end.

examples.ja: {質問|しつもん}を{減|へ}らしたいのではない。むしろ、{見|み}た{後|あと}で{話|はなし}を{掘|ほ}り{下|さ}げたい。
examples.en: I don’t want fewer questions. Rather, I want to explore them more deeply after watching.

examples.ja: これは{失敗|しっぱい}ではなく、むしろ{次|つぎ}の{工夫|くふう}につながる{経験|けいけん}だ。
examples.en: This isn’t a failure; it’s more an experience that can lead to improvements next time.

grammar.mistake: Do not infer that Mori opposes questions: the preferred order is film first, discussion afterwards.

grammar.title: Name the aspect on which the views agree
grammar.formation: Attributive clause + 点で; na-adjective + な点で; noun + の点で. A quoted description or noun phrase can be followed by という点で.
grammar.explanation: 点 names an aspect. 質問を大切にするという点で limits the agreement to valuing questions. The two authors still disagree about timing. Compare the same aspect on both sides; similarity on one point does not imply an identical proposal. という点で is useful when stating exactly what the shared point is.
grammar.example: 質問を大切にするという点で、二人の意見は同じだ。
grammar.translation: The two views agree in valuing questions.

examples.ja: {質問|しつもん}を{大切|たいせつ}にするという{点|てん}で、{二人|ふたり}の{意見|いけん}は{同|おな}じだ。
examples.en: The two views agree in valuing questions.

examples.ja: {止|と}める{時点|じてん}という{点|てん}で、{二|ふた}つの{案|あん}は{違|ちが}う。
examples.en: The two proposals differ in when to pause.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}が{明瞭|めいりょう}な{点|てん}で、この{案内|あんない}は{読|よ}みやすい。
examples.en: These instructions are easy to read because the explanation is clear.

grammar.mistake: Keep the named aspect attached. Agreement about questions does not mean both authors want to stop during the film.

dialogues.title: One pause, or every break?
dialogues.description: Yui wants questions while the film is fresh; Ren suggests limiting the interruptions.

lines.romaji: Shūmatsu no jōei, tochū de tomete mo ii kana.
lines.meaning: Would it be all right to pause the film at the weekend screening?

lines.speaker: Ren

lines.speaker: Ren

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {文章|ぶんしょう}には「{質問|しつもん}しやすい{一方|いっぽう}で、{流|なが}れが{途切|とぎ}れる」と{書|か}いた。

dialogues.title: Film first, questions afterwards
dialogues.description: Yui and Mori discuss short notes, replay and the order of the screening.

exercises.prompt: Where does Yui initially propose pausing?
options: At the end of the bakery section
In the middle of the owner’s voice
Before showing any of the film
exercises.explain: Yui names the end of the bakery part and explicitly says she does not want to interrupt someone speaking.

exercises.prompt: Why would Yui take questions there?
options: People can ask while they still remember the part
She wants to prevent all conversation after the film
She wants Ren to identify every photograph alone
exercises.explain: 覚えてるうちに聞いてほしくて gives her reason: asking while the memory is fresh.

options: Pause just once, not at every break
Remove the bakery part entirely
Stop the film after every sentence
exercises.explain: Ren suggests 全部の区切りじゃなくて、一回だけ. They will read Mori’s proposal before deciding.

exercises.line: {質問|しつもん}しやすい{一方|いっぽう}で、{話|はなし}の{流|なが}れが{途切|とぎ}れる。
exercises.prompt: Which two effects are held together?
options: Questions are easier, but the flow is interrupted
Questions are impossible, so the film is uninterrupted
Both authors have already approved one final schedule
exercises.explain: Both clauses remain true: easier questioning and interrupted flow. 一方で does not cancel the first clause.

exercises.context: Attach the taught 反面 directly to the na-adjective 有効: effective, but time-consuming.
exercises.line: この{方法|ほうほう}は{有効|ゆうこう}＿＿{反面|はんめん}、{時間|じかん}がかかる。
options: な
に
く
exercises.explain: A na-adjective takes な before 反面 here. である is another valid attachment but is not offered as a wrong answer.

exercises.line: {質問|しつもん}しやすい{反面|はんめん}、{映画|えいが}に{没頭|ぼっとう}しにくい。
exercises.prompt: What drawback does this sentence state?
options: It is harder to get absorbed in the film
The owner’s voice has been deleted
It is impossible for anyone to ask a question
exercises.explain: 没頭しにくい names a difficulty getting absorbed. The sentence still says questions are easier.

Show the whole film first, then replay selected parts
Ask for long written responses before the film
exercises.explain: The opening proposes breaks for questions. A single pause is later offered as an option for many first-time viewers, not a decided replacement.

exercises.prompt: What does Yui explicitly avoid interrupting?
options: The owner’s voice while it is playing
Every question after the screening
The preparation of paper and pens
exercises.explain: 店主の声が流れている途中では止めない is an explicit limitation on her proposal.

exercises.prompt: What would Yui do if the questions run long?
options: Take the remaining questions after the screening
Cancel every remaining question
Require only the archive staff to speak
exercises.explain: 質問が長くなったら、残りは上映の後に聞く. The proposal preserves later questions.

exercises.meaning: Constrained two-effect statement: questions are easier, while the flow is interrupted.
exercises.explain: The tiles preserve both effects of the same approach; this is not a free-expression fluency score.

Discuss every photograph before the film starts
Play only the last section
exercises.explain: Mori says 最後まで見てから話したい. The film is twelve minutes long.

exercises.prompt: How would Mori help people remember questions?
options: Give them paper for short notes
Tell them that questions are forbidden
Make Yui read every question during the film
exercises.explain: Mori suggests メモ用の紙. Yui will prepare paper and pens.

exercises.prompt: What does Mori say about replaying the bakery owner’s voice?
options: They can return to that part after watching the whole film
It must never be replayed
They will remove it before the event
exercises.explain: Mori agrees to go back to that part and invite memories. Mori’s preference is an order, not a ban on revisiting material.

exercises.line: {途中|とちゅう}で{止|と}めるより、むしろ{全編|ぜんぺん}を{先|さき}に{見|み}たい。
exercises.prompt: Which alternative does むしろ mark as preferred?
options: Watch the whole film first
Pause before watching every section
Do not watch the film at all
exercises.explain: The preferred alternative follows むしろ. The sentence does not by itself abolish discussion afterwards.

exercises.line: {質問|しつもん}を{大切|たいせつ}にするという{点|てん}で、{二人|ふたり}は{同|おな}じだ。
exercises.prompt: How far does the stated agreement extend?
options: They both value questions; the timing may still differ
Every detail of their proposals is identical
Both reject all questions during and after the film
exercises.explain: という点で identifies the shared aspect. It does not make their schedules identical.

exercises.prompt: Read both opinions. What do both authors want the event to provide?
options: A chance for people to ask questions and share memories
Silent viewing with no discussion afterwards
A long written response from every viewer
exercises.explain: A wants questions and shared memories at breaks and afterwards. B wants questions and discussion after the whole film. Their shared purpose is conversation.

exercises.prompt: Read both opinions. What is the central difference between the proposals?
options: Whether to pause at section breaks or show the whole film first
Whether the film concerns the shopping street or a railway
Whether the film is twelve minutes or two hours long
exercises.explain: Both discuss the same twelve-minute film. A favours section-break questions; B favours the whole film first, then discussion and selective replay.

exercises.prompt: Read both opinions. Which concern is assigned to the correct author?
options: A worries pauses interrupt immersion; B worries lengthy note-taking distracts from the images
A says nobody remembers questions; B says everyone must write an essay
A worries about a railway closure; B worries about the film’s ticket price
exercises.explain: A acknowledges flow and immersion may suffer. B explicitly notes that focusing too much on writing can make someone miss the images. Neither concern means the whole proposal is rejected.

exercises.prompt: Read both opinions. Which description of later questions is supported?
options: Both allow questions afterwards; B also proposes replaying needed parts
Only A allows any later questions; B forbids them
Both require every question to be asked before viewing
exercises.explain: A moves remaining questions after the screening if they take too long. B puts discussion afterwards and offers replay of selected parts.

exercises.explain: The sentence confines the agreement to a named aspect; it does not declare the proposals identical.

recycling.reason: The same twelve-minute documentary naturally retrieves 上映 and the recorded owner’s voice from unit 12. The supplementary comparison vocabulary is not forced into spoken lines; a four-percent recent-reference target preserves a realistic planning exchange.

grammar: two aspects: 一方で / 反面
watch.prompt: Optionally read two reviews or opinions about one film you know. Name one shared purpose, one real difference and one stated limitation in each. Keep the authors distinct; agreement on one aspect is not agreement on every detail.
